A friendship with a retired member of staff who has left the regulator
A membership of a local running club with no link to any regulated body
A subscription to a trade magazine covering the whole industry

questions.hint: Financial stakes in regulated bodies are a classic conflict.

items.title: L6: Probation and the first weeks
items.source: Civil Service Management Code; Civil Service Code; department induction guidance
items.body:
New civil servants normally serve a probation period set out in their contract or terms. During it the manager checks that you can do the job, behave in line with the Civil Service Code and meet attendance and conduct expectations. The length and the process vary by department, so read your own terms. Probation is a structured chance to show you are suitable, with regular one-to-ones, clear objectives and feedback. At the end the manager decides whether to confirm you in post, extend the period or, in some cases, end employment through the proper process.

In your first weeks, you usually complete mandatory learning, often covering security awareness, data protection, the Civil Service Code, diversity and inclusion, and health and safety. You may also sign declarations about the Official Secrets Act and about conflicts of interest. Do these promptly, since they are part of how you demonstrate you understand the rules.

Best habits are to agree objectives early, ask questions when unsure, report mistakes straight away, keep records of conversations about performance, and raise concerns about workload or support early. If you struggle, say so; managers can only help with what they know about. If you disagree with a probation decision, use the department's review or appeals process and the grievance procedure.

Probation is also the time to learn the culture: how decisions are made, how information is shared, how to escalate. Observing and asking are expected, not signs of weakness.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of probation?

options.text: To prepare staff for promotion to the next grade as soon as possible
To check suitability for the job and conduct, with structured feedback
To complete the security clearance process while the person is working
To pay a reduced wage while skills are built up and tested in the role

questions.hint: Probation is a structured period of assessment and support.

questions.prompt: Which outcomes are possible at the end of probation?

options.text: Automatic promotion to the next grade for everybody who completes it
Only dismissal, as probation is a trial and no other outcome is possible
Confirmation, an extension or, in some cases, ending employment through the proper process
Only confirmation, as probation can never be extended and is never failed

questions.hint: The manager can confirm, extend or end, depending on the process.

questions.prompt: Why should mandatory learning be completed promptly?

options.text: It is intended for senior staff, who carry the greatest responsibility for the rules
It replaces your objectives for the first months, so no other targets are set
It helps show that you understand the rules, and completing it is part of meeting the expectations of probation
It is optional and can be left until the end of the year without any consequence

questions.hint: Mandatory learning is part of demonstrating understanding of required standards.

questions.prompt: In week three you are struggling with workload. What is a sensible response?

options.text: Wait for the probation review to raise it, since that is the proper time for feedback
Say nothing and work late to catch up, so that nobody sees you are finding it hard
Hope it improves by itself, because the first weeks are always the hardest part
Tell your manager early so support can be arranged

questions.hint: Managers can only help with what they know about.

questions.prompt: You make an error in a document sent to a customer. What is the best action?

options.text: Wait to see whether anyone notices before you decide whether to say anything
Report it to your manager straight away and help to put it right with the customer
Fix it quietly and do not mention it, since the customer has not complained
Blame the template, because the template is the real source of the problem

questions.hint: Early honest reporting is expected.

questions.prompt: Why keep notes of conversations about your performance?

options.text: They give you a record if there is later disagreement
They replace your objectives, so you need not agree any others
They are shared with the whole team at the end of the probation period
They are required by law to be kept by every employee on probation

questions.hint: A personal record helps if there is a misunderstanding.

questions.prompt: What can you do if you disagree with a probation decision?

options.text: Ignore the decision and carry on as if it had not been made
Use the department's review, appeals or grievance process to put your case in the proper way
Resign immediately, since that is the only way to challenge a decision
Post about it online, so that others can judge whether it was fair

questions.hint: Formal routes exist for challenging decisions.

questions.prompt: Which declarations might you sign in the first weeks?

options.text: Ones about the Official Secrets Act and about conflicts of interest
Ones about your favourite hobbies, which are kept on the staff directory
Ones about your holiday plans and the dates on which you intend to take leave
Ones about your voting intention at the next general election

questions.hint: Common start-up declarations cover confidentiality and interests.

questions.prompt: Which statement about asking questions during induction is right?

options.text: Questions should be saved for the end of probation, when they will not distract
Asking questions suggests you are not ready for the job and may harm your review
Only managers are allowed to ask questions in the first weeks of employment
Asking questions and observing are expected, not signs of weakness

questions.hint: Learning the culture involves asking.

questions.prompt: Where will you find the length of your probation period?

options.text: On your security pass, which shows the date on which probation ends
On the department's homepage, which sets the period for every new starter
In your contract or terms of employment, which set out the period and how the process works
In the Official Secrets Act, which lays down the periods for all staff

questions.hint: The terms set out the period and process.

items.title: L6: Personal data and breaches in practice
items.source: UK GDPR and Data Protection Act 2018; ICO guidance on personal data breaches
items.body:
Civil servants handle personal data about the public and colleagues. The UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 require that personal data is used lawfully, fairly and transparently, only for the stated purpose, kept accurate, kept no longer than needed and held securely. You should only access personal data you need for your work, so looking up a neighbour, friend or ex-partner out of curiosity is misconduct and can be a criminal offence under the Data Protection Act.

A personal data breach is a security incident that leads to accidental or unlawful loss, alteration, disclosure of, or access to, personal data. Typical examples are an email to the wrong person, a lost laptop, a document left on a train, or an attachment containing more data than intended. Not every breach harms people, but all must be recorded.

Staff should report a suspected breach internally immediately, using the department's route, usually to a line manager, security team or data protection officer. The department decides whether to notify the Information Commissioner's Office, and the law generally requires notification within 72 hours of becoming aware where the breach is likely to put individuals at risk. Where the risk is high, the people affected may also need to be told. Delay in reporting inside the organisation can make the department miss the deadline.

When sending data, check recipients, use approved secure methods, and send the minimum needed. If you spot a recipient error after sending, do not try to fix it alone: report it so recall and containment are handled properly.

questions.prompt: A friend asks you to check whether their benefit claim has been paid. What should you do?

options.text: Look it up quickly as a favour, since you are only reading the data and not changing it
Decline and point them to the official channel
Look it up but tell nobody, so that nothing can be traced back to your friend
Ask a colleague to look it up instead, so that your own name is not on the record

questions.hint: Accessing data without a work need is misconduct and may be an offence.

questions.prompt: What counts as a personal data breach?

options.text: A security incident causing accidental or unlawful loss, alteration, disclosure or access to personal data
Any complaint from a customer about the way that their claim has been handled
Any system outage that lasts for more than an hour, whatever data was affected
Any late reply to a request for personal information from a member of the public

questions.hint: The definition covers loss, alteration, disclosure or access.

questions.prompt: You send an email with customer details to the wrong address. What is your first step?

options.text: Resend to the right address and say nothing, since that puts the matter right
Wait to see if the recipient replies, since a reply will show whether the mistake matters
Delete your sent copy, so that there is no record of the mistake on the system
Report it immediately through the department's route, without trying to deal with it alone

questions.hint: Immediate internal reporting enables containment and meeting deadlines.

questions.prompt: Why does delay in reporting internally matter?

options.text: It changes the data in the message, so that the damage becomes worse
It has no effect, because the clock starts only when the ICO is told
The department may miss the legal notification window
It makes the data public, because unreported incidents are published automatically

questions.hint: Notification has a short deadline from the moment of awareness.

questions.prompt: What is the general notification period to the ICO for a breach likely to put individuals at risk?

options.text: There is no set period, since the department can choose when to tell the ICO
Within 72 hours of the department becoming aware of the breach, where there is a likely risk to individuals
Within 30 days of the date on which the department completes its investigation
Within one year of the date on which the breach took place

questions.hint: The 72-hour rule is a well-known requirement.

questions.prompt: Which principle means data should be used only for the reason it was collected?

options.text: Purpose limitation
Storage limitation, because the data is kept only for the period needed
Accuracy, because the data must match the purpose for which it was collected
Integrity, because the data must not be changed without proper authority

questions.hint: Data should be used only for the stated purposes.

questions.prompt: Who decides whether the ICO is notified of a breach?

options.text: The individual member of staff who caused the breach, since they know the facts best
The affected customer, who must give permission before any report is made
The department, usually acting through its data protection officer, after the member of staff has reported it
The press office, which handles every contact with outside bodies

questions.hint: Staff report; the organisation decides on notification.

questions.prompt: You notice the recipient error after sending. Should you try to recall and fix it quietly?

options.text: Fix it quietly and keep the matter to yourself, since a successful recall means there is no breach
Fix it quietly, but send the recipient an apology so that they know it was a mistake
Wait until the end of the day, in case the recipient has not yet opened the message
Report it so recall and containment are done properly

questions.hint: Containment should be managed with the right people.

questions.prompt: Which action best reduces risk when emailing personal data?

options.text: Send from a personal account for speed, when the work system is slow
Send the whole file to be safe, so that nothing the recipient needs is left out
Copy in extra colleagues in case there are questions, so the data is not lost
Check the recipient, use approved secure methods and send only the minimum needed

questions.hint: Minimising and checking reduce exposure.

questions.prompt: What is the position on looking up an ex-partner on a work system?

options.text: It is misconduct, because the access has no work purpose, and it can be a criminal offence
It is acceptable if you tell nobody, because no one is harmed by a private look
It is acceptable if you do it only once, as a single look cannot cause serious harm
It is acceptable for senior staff, who are trusted with wider access

questions.hint: Accessing personal data for private reasons is not permitted.
